function: SAC agent chooses per-UE BS transmit power and beam codebook entries and RIS azimuth/elevation codebook entries, maximizing the minimum SINR under jamming (p. 10).
system: Downlink MU-MISO: 8-antenna ULA BS, 4 single-antenna UEs, 8-antenna jammer, passive reflecting RIS with 10x10 elements, blocked direct link; frequency band not stated (p. 3, p. 12).
method: Soft Actor-Critic deep reinforcement learning, six-layer fully connected policy and value networks, beam codebooks discretize actions; offline training from a replay buffer, online decisions (p. 9, p. 12).
data_channel: Custom simulator: Rician fading (K-factor 10 on RIS links), Gauss-Markov time correlation 0.85, path-loss exponents 2.2-3.8, UEs in a 10 m circle (p. 4, p. 12, p. 13).
test_conditions: Simulated K=4, M=8, N=100; sweeps over BS and jammer power, N, codebook size, time correlation and CSI error; no separate training and test conditions stated (p. 13-15).
baselines: AO optimization with SOCP and SDR (real-time, perfect or imperfect CSI), its relaxed upper bound, AO without RIS, sum-rate AO; no earlier learned method compared (p. 13-14).
metrics: Minimum SINR (dB) versus iterations, BS power, jammer power, N, codebook size, correlation, CSI error; sum rate and weakest-user rate; training time (p. 13-15).
complexity: Order of complexity of SAC training and inference in K, M, L, N, F, S (p. 12); training time versus codebook size (p. 15).
q1_support: p. 3: "a small-scale fading component that is assumed to follow the Rician fading model"
q2_support: p. 14: "we evaluate the performance against the number of reflecting elements and codebook vectors of the RIS"
q3_support: p. 3: "to serve as a benchmark solution, as there is currently no existing work on the max-min fairness problem"
q4_support: p. 12: "inference phase can be approximated as O (2 (K +1)"
q5_support: p. 4: "These channels are generated by following a similar procedure as the above description"
notes: Included, area 3: the SAC agent outputs the BS transmit power and beam codebook choice per UE and the RIS azimuth and elevation codebook choices (action space, Eq. 42, p. 10), i.e. precoder and RIS configuration. FUNCTION TO CONFIRM: 'anti-jamming' is in the exclusion list of step 1.5, but the learned output is beamforming and RIS phases (Algorithm 3 is titled 'Anti-Jamming Beamforming Design Based on SAC', p. 10); the jammer enters only through the SINR in the reward (Eq. 44, p. 11), and no jammer detection, frequency hopping or channel selection is learned. q1=0: custom Rician simulator, K-factor 10 on the RIS links (p. 3, p. 12), no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured data. q2=0: only sweeps over powers, N, codebook size, correlation and CSI error (p. 13-15); the paper never states a test in conditions unseen in training, and the state differs per CSI assumption (p. 10-11). q3=0: the benchmarks are the authors' own non-learned AO method, its relaxed bound and a no-RIS AO; earlier DRL anti-jamming RIS works [27] and [28] are discussed in related work (p. 3) but not compared in the results. q4=1: complexity orders of SAC training and inference (p. 12) and training time versus codebook size (Fig. 12, p. 15). q5=0: no code or data link; the only external link is the CVX toolbox (ref. [37]).
